figures.finding: A minor cannot contract (only a person of the age of majority is competent); for a child artist the producer must have the District Magistrate's permission with the parents' consent, and at least twenty per cent of the child's income from the production goes straight into a fixed deposit in a nationalised bank in the child's name, credited at majority; the actors' association and the producers' guild ask fifty per cent.

value.competent: of the age of majority (Contract Act s 11)
value.binding: District Magistrate's permission plus parental consent (CALPR Rules r 2C(1)(b))

law.where: fixed deposit in a nationalised bank in the child's name, credited at majority

CINTAA.where: fixed deposits or bonds maturing at 18

PGI.where: fixed deposit or bonds maturing at 18

figures.applies: Rule 2C reaches a child who works 'as an artist' in audio-visual media production or a commercial event; nothing found extends it to writing or directing. The central rules' text was not reached (India Code timed out); rule 2C is quoted from Puducherry's 2020 gazette, which copies it, marked secondary.

sources.said: Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject

at least twenty percent of the income earned by the child from the production or event to be directly deposited in a fixed deposit amount in a Nationalized Bank in the name of the child which may be credited to the child on attaining majority;
Provided that a minimum of 50% of the payment must be set aside for children in fixed deposits or bonds that mature when they reach the age of 18 years.

at least 50% amount payable to them towards their engagement/involvement in audio visual content/project should be set aside in the form of fixed deposit or bonds, maturing when they reach the age of 18 years.

figures.finding: The producer needs the District Magistrate's permission and files an undertaking valid six months; a child works at most five hours a day and three without rest, never more than twenty-seven days running, with one responsible person per five children and schooling kept up.

value.permit: permission of the District Magistrate of the district of the activity; undertaking in Form C/D valid 6 months
value.supervisor: one responsible person for at most five children

industry.CINTAA: no more than 10 school days missed in an academic year
industry.PGI: one shift a day, a break after every hour

figures.applies: Child artists (under fourteen; layer 3's work age) in audio-visual production or commercial events; adolescents of 14-17 fall under the Act's general rules (not read).

sources.said: no child shall be allowed to work for more than five hours in a day, and for not more than three hours without rest;
no child shall be allowed to work consecutively for more than twenty-seven days;
one responsible person be appointed for maximum of five children for the production or event,
The child should not miss school on account of shooting, for more than 10 days in an academic year work.
A child shall only participate in one shift per day, with a break after every hour.

figures.finding: CINTAA (Cine and TV Artistes Association) admits child artistes, anyone under eighteen, on a separate card; they cannot be life members, which needs eighteen.
figures.applies: Performers. The Screenwriters Association's and FWICE's rules were not read (blocker).

sources.said: Child Artiste: The child is defined as a person who is below 18 years of age. There will be separate design card for child artiste for easy identification.
Child artiste is not eligible for Life membership.

figures.finding: NFDC's Screenwriters' Lab takes Indian passport holders living in India or OCI cardholders; no age is stated.

NFDC-ScreenwritersLab2025.who: Indian passport holders residing in India or OCI cardholders

figures.applies: NFDC Screenwriters' Lab 2025 rules only; other NFDC programmes not read.

sources.said: The Screenwriters' Lab shall accept applications only from either Indian passport holders residing in India or from valid Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders.

figures.finding: A minor may not be the member of a one-person company, its nominee, or hold its shares beneficially; no age for a director of other companies was found in the texts reached.
figures.applies: Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, rule 3(4), as reproduced by ca2013.com (the MCA's own pages refused).

sources.said: (4) No minor shall become member or nominee of the One Person Company or can hold share with beneficial interest.
